documents.abstract: Using the observation that the side effects of aristeromycin (carbocyclic adenosine) were reduced by removing the methylene at the center in aristeromycin where phosphorylation occurs, derivatives of carbocyclic oxetanocin A (4a), oxetanocin G (4b), and 2-aminooxetanocin A (16) lacking the 3'-methylene have been prepared in racemic form. The only viruses for which an appreciable inhibitory effect of the compounds (minimum inhibitory concentration ranging from 1 to 40 microg/mL) was noted were herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) and varicella-zoster virus (VZV). However, when directly compared for their antiviral potency against HSV-1 with their parents oxetanocin A and oxetanocin G, compounds 4a and 4b proved clearly less active.
documents.authors: Wu J, Schneller SW, Seley KL.
documents.title: Carbocyclic oxetanocins lacking the C-3' methylene.
